blocks.body:
One of the easiest ways to clean up a desk setup is to move most of your cables underneath the desk.

An **under-desk cable management tray** gives you a dedicated place for power strips, laptop chargers, monitor adapters, and excess cable length.

Instead of having everything sitting on the floor or hanging behind your desk, the cables stay neatly hidden underneath the desktop.

Clamp-on cable trays are especially useful because many of them can be installed without drilling holes into your desk.

They work particularly well for setups with multiple monitors, computers, speakers, desk lamps, or other accessories that require several power cables.

### Why it helps

A cable tray keeps power bricks and cables off the floor, reduces visible clutter, and makes cleaning around your desk much easier.

![Under desk cable management tray for clean desk setup](/uploads/chatgpt-image-oct-3-2026-09_10_27-am-1.png)

blocks.heading: Install an Under-Desk Cable Management Tray

blocks.body:
Charging cables have a habit of disappearing behind the desk as soon as you unplug your phone.

A simple solution is to attach **magnetic cable clips** or cable holders near the edge of your desk.

These small organizers keep USB-C, Lightning, headphone, and other frequently used cables exactly where you need them.

Instead of reaching behind your desk every time you need a charger, the cable stays attached to the edge of your workspace.

Magnetic clips are also useful because you can quickly remove and reconnect the cable without permanently securing it.

For an even cleaner appearance, place several clips next to each other for your phone, tablet, headphones, or other accessories.

![Magnetic cable clips for organizing charging cables on desk](/uploads/chatgpt-image-oct-3-2026-09_10_30-am-2.png " Magnetic Cable Clips")

blocks.heading: Use Magnetic Cable Clips for Everyday Cables

blocks.body:
Even after installing a cable tray, you may still have several wires running between your desk and the floor.

Instead of allowing them to hang separately, bundle them together using a **cable management sleeve**.

A cable sleeve wraps multiple cables into one clean bundle, making your setup look much more organized.

They're especially helpful when several cables run in the same direction, such as monitor cables, PC power cords, Ethernet cables, speaker wires, or charging cables.

Black sleeves can blend naturally into darker desk setups, while white sleeves work well with lighter desks and walls.

The result is simple: instead of seeing five or six separate cables, you see one organized cable bundle.

![Cable management sleeve organizing multiple desk cables](/uploads/chatgpt-image-oct-3-2026-09_10_32-am-3.png " Cable Sleeve")

blocks.heading: Bundle Loose Wires With a Cable Sleeve

blocks.body:
Another source of desk clutter is having separate charging cables for your phone, smartwatch, earbuds, and other devices.

A **multi-device charging dock** can replace several individual chargers with one compact station.

A 3-in-1 charging station, for example, can keep your phone, wireless earbuds, and smartwatch charging in one place.

This doesn't just reduce cable clutter. It also creates a dedicated charging area so your devices aren't scattered around your workspace.

Place the charging station near the side or back of your desk and route its single power cable through your cable tray.

That gives you a much cleaner setup compared with having multiple charging cables running across the desktop.

![3 in 1 charging dock for clean desk cable management](/uploads/chatgpt-image-oct-3-2026-09_10_33-am-4.png "Charging Dock")

blocks.heading: Replace Multiple Chargers With a Charging Dock

blocks.body:
Sometimes the biggest source of cable clutter isn't the cables themselves.

It's the power strip.

Multiple plugs, large adapters, and excess cable length can make the area under or behind a desk look messy very quickly.

A **cable management box** hides the power strip and adapters inside a simple enclosed container.

Small openings on the sides allow cables to enter and exit while keeping most of the electrical clutter hidden.

You can place the box on the floor, behind your monitor, underneath your desk, or beside your workspace depending on your setup.

Pairing a cable box with an under-desk cable tray can make an especially big difference in a workspace with lots of electronics.

![Cable management box hiding power strip and desk cables](/uploads/chatgpt-image-oct-3-2026-09_10_34-am-5.png "Cable Management Box")
